runs.name: Hudson Technologies, Inc.
runs.box: TOO HARD (NATURE) AT Q2; integrity facts recorded, not judged
runs.entry: Price **$5.12** (close 2026-10-12, `tools/run.py`'s aggregator quote, flagged). Shares **42,088,547** (cover of the 10-Q for the quarter ended 2026-06-30, filed 2026-08-07, accession 0001104659-26-092682; one class, no treasury stock, repurchased shares retired; checked against the balance sheet; no later 8-K or prospectus; 3,039,889 options at $4.28 beside, about 7%); cap **$215.5M**. Sovereign **5.60%** (US Treasury par curve 30-year, 2026-10-09). Filing read: 10-K FY2025 filed 2026-03-16, accession 0001104659-26-028445, with the 10-Ks FY2018 to FY2024, the 10-Qs of 2026, the proxy of 2026-04-24 and the 8-Ks since 2025-08; one figure cross-checked (FY2025 operating cash -$3.16M tagged, "$3.2 million" used in the MD&A; inventory $135.9M). Lines of evidence derived by the analyst from the 10-K's Items 1, 1A and 7, as the overnight brief directs (refrigerant prices and the HFC phasedown, regulatory dependence, inventory, competition on price, the DLA at 15% of revenue, debt, the management change). Competitors: the 10-K names no rival in Items 1, 1A or 7 (FY2021 to FY2025), so no comparison; flagged. **Q1 IN** by the commodity routing (one segment; revenue is pounds times price per pound in every MD&A FY2018-25), the doubt on ten-year earning power (operating results from a $42.6M loss in FY2018 to $131.5M profit in FY2022) carried to Q2. **Q2 TOO HARD (NATURE)**: reclaimed gas sold to the same purity standard as virgin gas, competing on "price, particularly with respect to refrigerant sales"; no filing states the cost position and no rival is named; returns set by HFC prices and a regulator (Item 1A: "largely dependent upon continued regulation"; the EPA Technology Transition rule under reconsideration); the AIM Act's change for the better not credited until a full cycle in which price holds (Q2 2026 pricing -6%, "a continued trough in HFC market prices"); volume rose (pounds +12% in Q2 2026), written as contrary evidence. Q3 to Q12 not reached. Re-look condition in the box line: the first fiscal year in which Hudson's or the field's reported refrigerant volume falls. After the stop, recorded not weighed: inventory is the business ($135.9M of $318.6M assets at FY2025); the 2017 Airgas-Refrigerants purchase ($209M, debt-funded, about $167M owed at year-end 2017) was followed by a $35.9M inventory write-down in 2018 and covenant waivers in 2018-2019; equity $123.5M (2017) to $40.6M (2020), rebuilt to $243.4M; no borrowings since 2023, cash $25.6M at 2026-06-30, a $40M facility maturing 2027-03-02; buybacks at about $6.00-6.92; storm damage to the Champaign reclamation facility in June 2026, stated as expected to be insured; integrity facts recorded, not judged: the chief executive terminated without cause on 2025-11-03 (24 months' salary severance), a director who ran sales resigned 2026-03-13, the full-year 2026 gross-margin target cut in August 2026. COMPUTATION, NOT A CLEARANCE: owner cash after all capital spending, stock pay and acquisitions averaged **$32.1M** FY2021-25 equity-only ($35.8M all-equity), but only **$4.9M** FY2016-25 with the 2017 purchase deducted; **range $8.67 to $19.14 a share** all-equity on the FY2022-25 cycle base ($43.7M; decline -10.8% a year the bottom; literal window $7.22 to $15.81) against $5.12; floor tested first, both cases earn it at the price; fair price beneath the stop **$8.40 all-equity**, $9.54 equity-only; beside the convention, the ten-year record at no growth is about $5.25 a share at the government rate; not armed (box not OUT at Q7). Contamination declared by the analyst: session-context git status and commit subjects (HRIBF, AYI and ARCB research files), the memory index lines, one entry count of `Test Runs/` that printed no names; nothing on Hudson; none used. Commits aa6610f9, 1a487bd9, 9ab4f98f, 7bea3b2a, d98e156e. Citations: the analyst's check PASS; the dispatcher's adjacency script 38 distinct ids resolved, 0 E-ids, 28 adjacent fragments, 0 slips. Position note filled at the fold (not held). check_framework PASS. **For the operator:** the analyst's gaps: (1) whether a price a regulator makes (AIM Act allowances, EPA rules) is a "commodity price" for the routing that kept Q1 open; read the other way the file closes at Q1 TOO HARD (NATURE), same box; (2) whether "no filing states it" (NATURE) or "operators' reports not read" (WORK) governs when the 10-K names no rival and the brief limits rivals to those named; (3) specific (a) does not say how the cycle base counts a window with troughs at both ends (FY2021-24 $48.2M, FY2022-25 $43.7M, FY2021-25 $35.8M); (4) no place in the convention for a ruinous acquisition in the previous cycle once growth between cycles is meaningless; (5) the re-look trigger names a volume fall, but here volume rose as price fell, so it may never fire.
runs.narr: Q2 TOO HARD (NATURE): a refrigerant reclaimer and seller selling gas to the same purity standard as virgin gas and competing on price, whose cost position no filing states and whose 10-K names no rival; returns set by HFC prices and a regulator (AIM Act allowances, an EPA rule under reconsideration); the change for the better not credited until a full cycle in which price holds (2026 a continued price trough while pounds rose, written down as contrary evidence). Q1 IN by the commodity routing. COMPUTATION beneath the stop: owner cash $32.1M a year FY2021-25 but $4.9M FY2016-25 with the debt-funded 2017 Airgas-Refrigerants purchase deducted (2018 write-down, covenant waivers); range $8.67 to $19.14 a share against $5.12; fair $8.40 all-equity ($9.54 equity-only), not armed. After the stop: no debt since 2023; integrity facts recorded, not judged: the chief executive terminated without cause in November 2025, the 2026 gross-margin target cut.
